Commentary.Commentary: 137 to win for Pakistan. India defended 132 here against Australia. Looks like South Africa have got their semi final spot sealed. Stay tuned for the run chase.

Good bowling by Pakistan for most parts but the last 4 overs just let the game slip away. 45 runs came in those 24 balls and could cost them the World Cup. Diana Baig bowled her heart out, with figures of 4-1-19-2 while the others were decent too, except Aiman Anwer, who went for 43 in her 4 overs.

Coming to the innings, this is a very good score posted by the Protea Women. They started poorly, losing 2 wickets in the Powerplay but Marizanne Kapp and Mignon du Preez revived the innings with a decent stand. When both got dismissed in the span of 15 balls, it seemed like there was a collapse on the cards but Laura Wolvaardt's blinder got the team close to 140. She was playing a decent knock but the last 6 balls that she faced, she jut ran away.

Diana Baig has a chat with Melanie Jones. On her plans to bowl to Lizelle Lee, she says that it was pretty simple (does not tell it though). Adds that she told herself before the game that she would dismiss Lee and is happy that she did. On the pitch today, Baig says that normally there is good bounce in Canberra but today was not the case. So she took 5 minutes to adjust to the track. On bowling 3 overs in the Powerplay, Diana says that in this World Cup, she has been in good rhythm, hence she bowled those many overs in the fielding restrictions.

FOUR! What a finish. Half century for Wolvaardt, in 36 balls. 5 boundaries in the last 6 balls she faced. Outstanding cricket, really terrific batting. Outside off, Laura reaches out and carves it over covers! Hugs her partner and both are smiles. This is a very, very good score. SOUTH AFRICA FINISH ON 136/6!
FOUR! Outstanding batting. Full and outside off, Wolvaardt backs away and lofts this over the covers!
FOUR! Good batting. Full on middle, Wolvaardt comes down the track and lofts it over the bowler through mid on!
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Trisha Chetty walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! Sensational catch by Aliya Riaz. Full and outside off, Tryon looks to play the slog sweep but gets a massive top edge. Initially it looks like it will land safely but Riaz keeps her sights on the ball at long on, comes running in, dives and takes a stunner!
Full and outside off, Tryon looks to drive through the covers but the slow pitch makes the ball comes slowly which induces an inside edge. The ball travels to long on and a couple of runs are taken.
FOUR! MAGNIFICENT! Full and outside off, Wolvaardt shows her class again, reaching out and driving through the covers! 15 from the over, is 140 still on?
FOUR! Excellent batting. Full and outside off, Wolvaardt gives herself room to the leg side and lofts it over extra cover, wide of long off!
Yorker, on middle, dug out to the leg side for a quick single.
FOUR! Fine shot. Full and around off, Tryon lofts it straight back over the bowler for a boundary!
Outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Full and outside off, swung over mid-wicket. Straight to the fielder. Just a single.
Outside off, played straight to short third man.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

DROPPED! AND A RUN OUT MISSED! Poor cricket. Full and outside off, Tryon gets across and swings this towards deep mid-wicket.  Diana Baig does all the hard work of coming running in from the deep. But then, when the ball makes contact with her hand, it spills out. Tryon takes the first run and then wants the second. But there is no communication with her partner. She is halfway down the track when she is sent back but the throw is a poor one to the bowler and she gets back.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for one.
Full and on middle, Tryon comes down the track and looks to flick but gets a leading edge over the bowler. A run taken.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Anam Amin to bowl. 2-0-4-0 so far.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a single. 12 runs and a wicket from the over. Aiman's figures read 3-0-28-1.
Chloe Tryon walks in at number 7, replacing Luus.

OUT! CAUGHT! Luus departs. Full and outside off, Sune looks to slog across the line but gets a top edge. Two fielders converge - short fine leg and short mid-wicket but the calling is clear. Umaima Sohail from the latter position tells it is hers and takes it.
Outside off, on a length, Luus backs away and carves it over cover. The fielder at short extra leaps for the catch but cannot reach the ball. Two runs taken.
On middle, punched down to long on for a single. 100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA. 21 balls left. 140 on the cards?
FOUR! Another boundary. South Africa are turning it on. Short and outside off, Wolvaardt lashes out the cut but gets a thick outside edge which flies behind point.
FOUR! LOVELY! What a shot. Full and outside off, Wolvaardt reaches out and drives it through extra cover. Long off tries to get around but the timing is excellent to beat her!
Aiman Anwer returns. 2-0-16-0 so far.
Full and down the leg side, swept through square leg for a couple.
WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Over the top. Mid off was up and Wolvaardt takes advantage. Full and outside off, Laura reaches out and lofts it over mid off.
Full and around middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full around off, whipped back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Down the leg side, tickled really fine. Good work by the short fine leg fielder to stop the boundary. Three runs taken. Sensational stuff by Diana. 4-1-19-2.
Punches this off the back foot for a run.
Short and outside off, slapped through the covers for one.
Full and around off, well defended.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, worked past short mid-wicket, wide of long on for a single.
Diana Baig to bowl out. 3-1-13-2 so far.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a single to end the over.
Full and around off, driven towards long on for one more.
Full and around off, pushed past short mid-wicket for another single.
Outside off, driven towards long off for one.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Nothing much on the Free Hit. Landed outside off, Wolvaardt slices it over point for a couple.
FREE HIT COMING UP!

Full and around off, watchfully pushed down the track. Wait a second. NO BALL signalled as one extra fielder was inside the 30-yard circle. You are allowed to have only four. The third umpire communicated the same to the on-field umpire.
Short and outside off, slapped through the covers for a run. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, Aroob finished with figures of 4-0-25-1.
Full and outside off, whipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Sune Luus walks in at number 6, replacing Kapp.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is given away. Kapp comes down the track and Aroob fires a full toss. A high one at that. Marizanne is surprised and looks to go over the top but is cramped for room slightly. Mistimes it and Iram Javed takes it calmly at long off. That is a big, big wicket. Both set batters dismissed in the span of 15 balls.
Fuller and outside off, Wolvaardt reaches out and plays it with the lack of bounce through mid-wicket, via a sweep. A single taken.
Fuller, around off, whipped to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover this time.
Good fielding. Wolvaardt reaches out and looks to drive through the covers but gets a thick outside edge to short third man where the fielder dives to her left and stops.

Very full, on leg stump, Kapp misses her flick and is hit on the pads. The ball deflects to the leg side and the batters take a late call to run. The bowler gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end. But unfortunately for her, it hits Kapp's bat and deflects away.
Full again, outside off, spinning in, worked to long on for a run.
Full and around middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, guided with the turn to short third man for another single.
That barely bounced. Short and outside off, scoots low, played nicely through the covers for one.
Outside off, hit down to long off for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Short and outside off, punched down to long on for a single.
Laura Wolvaardt walks in at number 5, replacing du Preez.

OUT! BOWLED! Oh dear... that took ages to arrive. Full and outside off, du Preez looks to play the reverse sweep but the ball comes on very slowly, spins in and by that time, the shot is already through. The ball hits the glove, then the front pad and deflects onto the off stump. End of a reviving 37-run stand.
FOUR! Hammered straight back. Full and on middle, du Preez lofts it down the ground. Long on cannot cut it off to her left.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Comes down the track and defends.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and around middle, chipped down to long on for a single.
Nida Dar to bowl now.
Punches this off the back foot for a run.
FOUR! Full and outside off, du Preez reverse sweeps it through third man!
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Outside off, driven through the covers for three runs.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full on middle, driven towards mid on.
Works this through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
SIX! That is a terrific shot. Full and down the leg side, this is whipped with the breeze over mid-wicket!
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Short and outside off, cut through the covers for a couple.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.

FOUR! Terrific shot, great effort but unlucky in the end. Du Preez cuts this between backward point and short third man. The fielder from short third man chases it down, pulls it back but the ball trickles back.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Full and outside off, Kapp hammers this straight to short extra cover and the power forces Javeria Khan to misfield. A single to long off.
Landed outside off, spinning away, punched straight to cover.
Fuller, just outside off, watchfully defended towards cover.
Short and outside off, spinning away, cut through the covers for a single.
Syed Aroob Shah to bowl now. A leg spinner.
FOUR! That is a good way to end the Powerplay. Full and down the leg side, Kapp flicks it over mid-wicket and finds the boundary. 23/2 in the Powerplay.
Short again, punched through the covers for a single.
Short and outside off, punched towards cover.
Around off, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Punches this through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to cover.
Aiman Anwer to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.
A back foot defense to end a WICKET MAIDEN! 3-1-13-2 for Diana so far.
Full and around off, driven towards mid on.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Mignon du Preez walks in next.

OUT! BOWLED! She has dragged it on. No review needed this time. A length ball, outside off, van Niekerk looks to hammer it through the off side but there is no feet movement. This is a cross-seam delivery. So it comes on a touch slower. All these factors contribute to an inside edge. The stumps are hit. The ploy to give Baig an extra over works.
Full and around off, punched back towards mid on.
Full and around off, driven back to the bowler who fumbles but no run taken.
Works this through mid-wicket for one more.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Flicks this through mid-wicket for a single.

Flicks this uppishly but gets it well wide of the fielder at square leg. The fielder chases it down, slides and stops the ball but returns a poor throw. That makes the third run easy. But the umpire says that it is ONE SHORT.
FOUR! Fine shot. Full on middle, Kapp hammers it straight back over the bowler!
WIDE. Second of the over. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Comes down the track and defends.
Full and around off, driven back to the bowler.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
WIDE. Full and well down the leg side, van Niekerk looks to sweep but misses.

NOT OUT! Well, well, well. Did we say plumb? Not at all, as per technology. That is why, we are not made for umpiring. A length ball, straight enough, van Niekerk gets across her stumps and looks to flick but misses. An appeal goes up and trust me, it does look plumb. But the non-striker does not feel so. She coolly asks her partner to take the review. There seems to be a technology failure and for that period, van Niekerk's heart would have been in her mouth. Because if it does not arrive, then the umpire's call would stay! But after nearly 5 minutes, they manage to get the technology working. First, Ultra Edge. Nothing on it. Now, Ball Tracker. Missing leg!
Dane van Niekerk has been adjudged LBW! She has taken the review though. After an age, technology starts working. Ball Tracker shows it to be MISSING LEG!
Full on middle, driven back to the bowler who fumbles but no run taken.

WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Full and around off, well blocked out.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! A boundary and a wicket from the opening over. Full and outside off, Lee, like she did on the first ball of the over, goes for the drive. That time, she missed. This time, she nicks. Simple catch for the keeper.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! AUDACIOUS! Full and wide outside off, Lee leans and lofts it over cover for a boundary! First of the game.
Full and outside off, this is driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, swinging away, Lee looks to drive but misses.

We are done with the anthems. The players are back out in the middle. Diana Baig will start off proceedings for the game. Lizelle Lee and Dane van Niekerk are the openers for the Saffas. Lee to face. Here we go...
Time for the national anthems. Pakistan's first up.

PITCH REPORT - Charlotte Edwards observing the pitch says that this is the same one which featured the Australia-India game of the tournament but also adds that the groundsmen have told here that this one would be a bit more pacy. Sees that there is no grass on the deck and predicts turn.

Pakistan skipper, Javeria Khan, says that she too, wanted to bat first. Is disappointed that Bismah Maroof is missing out but wants the other players to step up. On taking over the captaincy reigns in her 100th T20I, Khan says that it nothing new to her as she has taken captaincy in the past and she does not enjoy it one bit. Informs that there are two changes in the side. Syed Aroonb Shah comes in place of the injured Bismah Maroof while Sadia Iqbal has been rested and Anam Amin has been drafted in.

South African skipper, Dane van Niekerk, says that there will be something on the wicket first up but then could get slow as the game progresses. Informs that Marizane Kapp is back into the side  in place of Nadine de Klerk. On the promotion of Lizelle Lee, van Niekerk smiles and says that if she can play the way she did the other day against 90 percent of the games would be great. Says that win and go through to the semis sounds simple on paper but it isn't.
TOSS - The flip of the coin has gone Dane van Niekerk's way. SOUTH AFRICA WILL BAT FIRST.

Hello and a warm welcome to game number 15 of the T20 World Cup in 2020. Today can be called as quarterfinals day. Win and you go through to the semis. Lose and you wait for another year to try and win the World Cup. South Africa meet Pakistan now, followed by the West Indies-England clash at the Sydney Showground Stadium.
